title: Secure Signal Admin API
description: REST API for the Secure Signal Admin Next.js app. Staff/rider routes use Supabase session cookies (sb-access-token / sb-refresh-token). Device-facing routes (mobile app → backend) use a separate shared-secret header instead — there's no user session on the device. Role checks: admin > authority > seller/rider.

conventions.auth: Browser-side Supabase session cookie for staff/rider routes. Unauthed -> 401 {error:"unauth"}. Device routes require the X-Device-Key header instead (see deviceAuth below); missing/wrong -> 401, server not configured -> 503.
conventions.errors: JSON { error: string } unless noted. Validation errors on most routes include an `issues` array.
conventions.rateLimiting: Fixed-window, backed by Postgres (see rateLimits below). Exceeding it returns 429 { error: "too many requests" }. Fails open on infra error — never blocks a request over a rate-limiter outage.

rbac.admin: Full access; admin-only routes check profile.role === 'admin'.
rbac.authority: May patch incident status, send/start/stop device pings, message riders.
rbac.seller: Manages own business profile (services, hours, service area) via onboarding.
rbac.rider: May manage own emergency contacts, read own incidents, self-delete account.

deviceAuth.notes: Required on every device-facing endpoint: /api/incidents/report, /api/incidents/log, /api/devices/register, PATCH /api/ping, and the legacy /api/incident + /api/incident/[id]/track POST endpoints. The value is the DEVICE_API_KEY env var configured on the server — request it from whoever manages the deployment. Compared with a constant-time check server-side.

routes.description: OAuth callback. Exchanges `code` for a Supabase session and redirects to `next` (defaults to /). On failure redirects to /login?error=oauth.

Register or confirm a device_uuid belongs to a user_id, optionally saving its current FCM push token into devices.fcm_id. Idempotent: a matching (device_uuid, user_id) pair already on file is a no-op beyond refreshing fcm_id if a new token is sent (e.g. after the OS rotates it), not a duplicate. If device_uuid exists under a *different* user_id, ownership is deliberately not reassigned (a `note` field is returned instead) — an unauthenticated device call shouldn't be able to silently hijack a device's owner; fcm_id still refreshes in that case since a token refresh is a device-level fact independent of ownership.

postRequest.device_uuid: string (required) — the hardware's own id, not a uuid
postRequest.user_id: string (required) — driver's profiles.id; degrades to null if unresolvable, never fails the request
postRequest.fcm_token: string (optional) — current FCM push token, saved to devices.fcm_id

responses.200: { data: device, created: false, note?: string }

routes.description: Strict update of devices.fcm_id for the row matching BOTH device_uuid AND user_id exactly. Unlike POST /api/devices/register (an upsert, lenient about ownership mismatches), this never creates a row — no match means 404. Meant for an already-registered device refreshing its own token, not first-time registration.

postRequest.user_id: string (required) — must resolve to a real profiles.id, or this 404s

responses.404: { error:"device not found for this user" }

postRequest.status: string (optional) — received | reported | canceled, default reported
postRequest.incident_type: string (optional) — SOS Button | SOS Volume keys | SOS USB | SOS Fall Detected; anything else stored as null rather than rejected

Hard-deletes the auth user, cascading to profile/emergency_contacts/subscriptions/seller_profiles/sent incident_messages and the profile_images storage folder. devices/incidents/logs are anonymized (user_id set null), not deleted, per the schema's existing retention design.

notes: incidents.device_id / incident_logs.device_id are text columns holding the hardware's own device_uuid directly — not a uuid FK to devices.id, despite the column name.

FCM push notification bodies are a client-parsed contract, not just display text: stop standard pings = 'STOP-{uuid}', start standard pings = 'STAR-{uuid}' (not a typo), stop emergency = 'STOP_EMERGENCY-{uuid}'.
